children: said Monday it received an order to supply optical components for U.S. government satellite constellations supporting Space Force infrastructure and reconnaissance operations.

The Rochester, New York-based optics manufacturer described the contract as the most significant order in its 25-year history, though it didn't disclose the value of the individual order or provide a delivery schedule.

said its optics will be used in satellite constellations associated with the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, or NRO. Information collected by the satellites can be used by the U.S. Space Force and other military branches.The NRO is expanding constellations consisting of larger numbers of satellites, an approach designed to increase coverage and reconnaissance revisit rates while reducing reliance on individual spacecraft.
said its optical technology is designed to operate under the temperature extremes encountered in space and support real-time tracking and observation of targets on Earth.
The company has previously produced thousands of optical components for satellite communications systems, including laser-based connections that allow satellites to communicate with one another.

Syntec also said it is developing a financial model for its space product lines based on a backlog exceeding $100 million. The company didn't specify how much of that backlog is associated with the newly announced order or provide details about the timing of potential revenue recognition.
The order expands Syntec's exposure to government space and defense programs as the U.S. continues to build out satellite-based reconnaissance and communications capabilities.

For investors, the size and timing of revenue associated with the contract remain key unknowns. While Syntec characterized the order as its most significant to date, the announcement didn't disclose its dollar value, expected margins or the period over which the work will be completed.
